newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures post hefty gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures post hefty gains.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures posted hefty gains on Tuesday in buoyant activity as the dollar rose to above 120 yen in late-afternoon Tokyo trade, traders said.
The August, October and December silver futures had risen by their six-yen-per-10-grams daily limit by the close, with the benchmark December ending at 192.4 yen.

The spot January gold contract expired at noon up 18 yen at 1,368 yen, with 136 lots of deliveries. Other gold futures ranged from 22 yen to 24 yen per gram up, with benchmark the December ending up 24 yen at 1,364 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $356.60/7.10 per ounce at 0724 GMT, against $356.00/365.50 in New York on Monday.

Spot gold sagged slightly in early Tokyo trade, pressured partly by Japanese selling in arbitrage dealing, but animated options-related buying by overseas funds later in the day helped spot gold reverse early losses, traders said.

"Gold may test $360 per ounce in the near-term, based on views that gold found a floor for the near-term. We are watching the U.S. financial markets for possible further corrections," one trader said.

In the gold and silver futures, private investors were liquidating long positions, locking in profits for most of the day, while trade houses bought futures while selling spot gold and silver in arbitrage trade.
Platinum futures rose double-digit gains on the heels of gold, while profit-taking put a lid on palladium futures after three distant months hit their life-of-contract highs earlier in the day.
Benchmark December platinum was up 17 yen per gram at 1,371 yen. Benchmark December palladium was up one yen at 469 yen.
